test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jul 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Through thick and thin

options.text: In good times and in bad times

solution:
The correct answer is: **In good times and in bad times**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**through thick and thin**" means to support someone or something consistently, even during difficult times.

 
 
• **For example**: *She supported her best friend through thick and thin, always being there in times of difficulty and happiness.*
 
 
 
• The phrase is often used to describe a strong and enduring friendship or relationship.
 
• The word "thick" refers to dense or difficult situations, while "thin" refers to times of scarcity or hardship.
 
• The phrase can also be used to describe someone's loyalty or commitment.

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Only assist during good times**" is incorrect because the idiom implies support during both good and bad times.
 
• "**Hope during trying times**" is not the best fit for the idiom, as it does not capture the idea of consistent support.
 
• "**Weak and lonely**" is not related to the meaning of the idiom.
